title: Reactions of Alkenes
content:
# Reactions of Alkenes

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Describe addition reactions of alkenes
- Write equations for reactions with hydrogen, water, and halogens
- Explain hydration and hydrogenation
- Understand the mechanism of electrophilic addition

## Introduction

The C=C double bond in alkenes is reactive and undergoes **addition reactions**. In these reactions, the double bond "opens up" and atoms add to the two carbon atoms. This is the basis for making many useful products.

## Key Concepts

### What Are Addition Reactions?

**In an addition reaction:**
- The double bond breaks open
- Atoms/groups add to the two carbon atoms
- Only one product is formed
- No atoms are lost

[DIAGRAM: General addition reaction showing C=C + X-Y → C-C with X and Y attached]

### Addition of Hydrogen (Hydrogenation)

**Conditions:**
- Nickel catalyst
- Temperature: 150°C
- Pressure: moderate

**General equation:**
$$\text{Alkene} + \text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni catalyst}} \text{Alkane}$$

**Example - Ethene to ethane:**
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4 + \text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni, 150°C}} \text{C}_2\text{H}_6$$

**Uses:**
- Making margarine from vegetable oils
- Hardening unsaturated fats

| Reactant | Product |
|----------|--------|
| Ethene + H₂ | Ethane |
| Propene + H₂ | Propane |
| Vegetable oil + H₂ | Margarine |

### Addition of Water (Hydration)

**Conditions:**
- Steam (H₂O)
- Phosphoric acid catalyst (H₃PO₄)
- High temperature (300°C)
- High pressure (60-70 atm)

**General equation:**
$$\text{Alkene} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4} \text{Alcohol}$$

**Example - Ethene to ethanol:**
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4, 300°C}} \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$$

This is the **industrial method** for making ethanol.

### Addition of Halogens (Halogenation)

**Conditions:**
- Room temperature
- No catalyst needed
- Alkene reacts with Cl₂, Br₂, or I₂

**General equation:**
$$\text{Alkene} + \text{Halogen} \rightarrow \text{Dihalogenoalkane}$$

**Example - Ethene with bromine:**
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Br}_2$$

Ethene + Bromine → 1,2-dibromoethane

**This is the test for unsaturation:**
- Bromine water: orange → colourless

### Addition of Hydrogen Halides

**Alkenes react with HCl, HBr, HI:**

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4 + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}$$

Ethene + Hydrogen bromide → Bromoethane

### Summary of Addition Reactions

| Reactant added | Product | Conditions |
|----------------|---------|------------|
| H₂ | Alkane | Ni catalyst, 150°C |
| H₂O | Alcohol | H₃PO₄ catalyst, 300°C, high pressure |
| Br₂ | Dibromoalkane | Room temperature |
| Cl₂ | Dichloroalkane | Room temperature |
| HBr | Bromoalkane | Room temperature |

### Electrophilic Addition Mechanism

**Step 1:** The electron-rich C=C attracts the electrophile (e.g., Br₂)

**Step 2:** The double bond breaks, one carbon bonds to Br, forming a carbocation

**Step 3:** The second Br⁻ bonds to the positively charged carbon

[DIAGRAM: Mechanism showing curly arrows for bromine addition to ethene]

**Why electrophilic addition?**
- **Electrophile:** electron-loving species (attracted to the C=C)
- **Addition:** atoms add across the double bond

### Markovnikov's Rule (Extension)

When HX adds to an unsymmetrical alkene:
- H adds to the carbon with more hydrogens already attached
- X adds to the carbon with fewer hydrogens

**Example with propene + HBr:**
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHBr}\text{CH}_3$$

The major product is 2-bromopropane (not 1-bromopropane)

## Worked Examples

**Example 1:** Write the equation for the reaction of propene with hydrogen.

**Solution:**
$$\text{C}_3\text{H}_6 + \text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni}} \text{C}_3\text{H}_8$$

- Propene + Hydrogen → Propane
- Conditions: Nickel catalyst, 150°C
- The double bond opens and H₂ adds across it

---

**Example 2:** Describe how ethanol is made industrially from ethene.

**Solution:**
- Ethene is reacted with steam (water vapour)
- Conditions: 300°C, 60-70 atm pressure
- Phosphoric acid (H₃PO₄) catalyst is used
- The reaction is:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$$
- This is called **hydration**
- The process is reversible; not all ethene converts
- Unreacted ethene is recycled

---

**Example 3:** Name the product when but-1-ene reacts with chlorine.

**Solution:**
- But-1-ene: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃
- Chlorine adds across the double bond
- Cl₂ becomes two Cl atoms, one on each carbon
- Product structure: CH₂ClCHClCH₂CH₃
- Product name: **1,2-dichlorobutane**

---

**Example 4:** Explain why vegetable oils are hydrogenated to make margarine.

**Solution:**
- Vegetable oils contain unsaturated fats (C=C bonds)
- These make the oil liquid at room temperature
- Adding hydrogen (H₂) across the double bonds creates saturated fats
- Saturated fats have higher melting points
- The hydrogenated fat is solid at room temperature
- This makes it spreadable as margarine
- Conditions: nickel catalyst, heat, hydrogen gas

## Common Mistakes

- **Mistake:** Confusing hydration (adding H₂O) with hydrogenation (adding H₂)
- **Correct:** Hydration makes alcohols; hydrogenation makes alkanes

- **Mistake:** Forgetting the catalyst in reaction conditions
- **Correct:** Ni for hydrogenation; H₃PO₄ for hydration

- **Mistake:** Thinking bromine water test shows a reaction with alkanes
- **Correct:** Alkanes don't react with bromine water (stays orange)

## Practice Questions

1. Write the equation for the reaction of ethene with hydrogen. State the conditions. (3 marks)

2. Name and draw the structure of the product when propene reacts with bromine. (3 marks)

3. Describe how ethanol is manufactured from ethene, including conditions. (4 marks)

4. Explain why the reaction between ethene and bromine is called an addition reaction. (2 marks)

5. Write the equation for the reaction of but-1-ene with hydrogen chloride. (2 marks)

6. Explain why margarine production involves reacting vegetable oils with hydrogen. (3 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Addition reaction | A reaction where atoms add across a double bond |
| Hydrogenation | Addition of hydrogen to an unsaturated compound |
| Hydration | Addition of water to a compound |
| Halogenation | Addition of a halogen to an unsaturated compound |
| Electrophile | A species attracted to regions of high electron density |

## Summary

- **Addition reactions:** Double bond opens, atoms add to both carbons
- **Hydrogenation:** Alkene + H₂ → Alkane (Ni catalyst, 150°C)
- **Hydration:** Alkene + H₂O → Alcohol (H₃PO₄, 300°C, high pressure)
- **Halogenation:** Alkene + Br₂ → Dibromoalkane (room temp, no catalyst)
- **Mechanism:** Electrophilic addition (electrophile attacks electron-rich C=C)
- **Uses:** Making ethanol, margarine, polymers, other chemicals
